title: Snap Fitness vs Jetts NZ — 24/7 Budget Gym Comparison 2026
meta_desc: Compare Snap Fitness and Jetts NZ 2026: weekly fees, contracts, locations and equipment to find the best 24/7 budget gym for Kiwi fitness fans.
intro: Both Snap Fitness and Jetts dominate the 24/7 budget gym market in New Zealand, but their pricing structures and contract commitments differ enough to sway the savvy Kiwi. This guide breaks down the real costs, locations and gear so you can pick the best value for your workout routine.

sections.heading: Quick Snapshot
sections.body: Snap Fitness offers a slightly lower no‑contract rate but a higher weekly fee for long‑term contracts, while Jetts keeps its pricing simple with a flat weekly rate and a modest discount for a 12‑month commitment.

sections.heading: Location Coverage
list: Snap Fitness: ~30 clubs – Auckland (10), Wellington (4), Christchurch (5), Hamilton (3), Tauranga (2), Dunedin (2), other regional towns (4).
Jetts NZ: ~20 clubs – Auckland (7), Wellington (3), Christchurch (4), Hamilton (2), Palmerston North (1), Nelson (1), other regional towns (2).

sections.heading: Equipment & Facility Highlights
list: Both chains provide 24/7 keycard access and unlimited cardio machines (treadmills, ellipticals, rowing).
Snap Fitness has a larger selection of plate‑loaded machines and a dedicated strength zone with squat racks and deadlift platforms.
Jetts focuses on functional training – open floor space, TRX straps, kettlebell banks and a free‑weight area that’s slightly larger per club.
Both offer free Wi‑Fi, locker rooms with showers, and a limited number of complimentary group classes per month (Snap: 2, Jetts: 1).

sections.heading: Contract Terms & Extras
list: Snap Fitness: No joining fee for online sign‑up; 12‑month contract incurs a $150 early termination fee; 24‑month contract reduces weekly rate to $12.95 (not included in table).
Jetts NZ: $0 joining fee during promotional periods; 12‑month contract can be cancelled with 30‑day notice and a $75 exit fee; no lock‑in for week‑to‑week members.
Both chains allow members to freeze their account for up to 30 days per year at no extra cost.

sections.heading: Bottom Line – Which Gives Better Value?
sections.body: If you’re comfortable with a 12‑month commitment and want the lowest weekly cost, Jetts edges out Snap by a few dollars per week and offers a simpler exit fee. Snap, however, provides more machines and a cheaper 24‑month option for those willing to lock in longer. Your decision should hinge on whether equipment variety or the absolute lowest price matters more.
